He is a 6-foot 10-inch, 265-pound [[Center (basketball)|center]] who played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]]. ==High school career== Orton played for [[Bishop McGuinness High School (Oklahoma)|Bishop McGuinness High School]] in Oklahoma City. Bishop McGuinness won the class 4A state championship Orton's freshman, sophomore, and junior year.{{cite web|url=http://www.ossaa.com/Sports/Basketball/HistoryofBasketball.aspx |title=State Boys Basketball Champions |work=OSSAA |access-date=September 4, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101007081746/http://ossaa.com/Sports/Basketball/HistoryofBasketball.aspx |archive-date=October 7, 2010 }} During his senior season, he tore his [[anterior cruciate ligament]] in his knee, cutting his final season of high school basketball short. He averaged 14 points, 11 rebounds and 5 blocks per game as a junior. Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Orton was listed as the No. 4 center and the No. 22 player in the nation in 2009.[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Daniel-Orton-51353;_ylt=Al.5WJ6S6VVsM1fVrn3lPhpGPZB4 Daniel Orton Recruiting Profile] He was recruited to the University of Kentucky by [[Billy Gillispie]]; however, Gillispie was fired following Orton's senior season. Orton kept his commitment to Kentucky after [[John Calipari]] was hired by the university. ==College career== Orton was a reserve on the 2009–10 Kentucky Wildcats basketball team, where he averaged 3.4 points, 3.3 rebounds, and 1.4 blocks in 13.2 minutes per game. On May 8, 2010, Orton hired an agent and declared himself eligible for the [[2010 NBA draft]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.courier-journal.com/article/20100508/SPORTS03/5080352/It-s-official-Kentucky-s-Eric-Bledsoe-Daniel-Orton-will-stay-in-NBA-draft|title=It's official: Kentucky's Eric Bledsoe, Daniel Orton will stay in NBA draft}} ==Professional career== With the 29th overall picking the first round of [[2010 NBA draft]], the [[Orlando Magic]] selected Daniel Orton. On July 1, 2010, Orton signed his rookie contract with the Magic.{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120917110605/http://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/daniel-orton-signs-magic-contract-20100701,0,1605188.story|title=Daniel Orton signs Orlando Magic contract}} On December 1, 2010, it was announced that Orton would be sent to the [[Canton Charge|New Mexico Thunderbirds]] of the [[NBA Development League]].[https://www.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/nba/2010-12-01-4199974517_x.htm Magic assign first-round pick Orton to D-League] USA Today, December 1, 2010 In his second game for the Thunderbirds, Orton suffered a season-ending knee injury. Orton made his NBA debut on January 27, 2012, in a Magic loss to the [[New Orleans Hornets]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.orlandopinstripedpost.com/2012/1/27/2753823/magic-hornets-score-recap-dwight-howard|title=New Orleans Hornets 93, Orlando Magic 67|first=Evan|last=Dunlap|date=January 27, 2012|website=Orlando Pinstriped Post}} On April 15, 2012, in a win against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], Orton scored a career-high 11 points while also recording 5 steals, 4 rebounds, and 3 blocks. In 16 games, he averaged 2.8 points per game. He played his first career playoff game against the [[Indiana Pacers]]. On August 4, 2012, Orton was signed by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Daniel Orton|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/release_orton_120804.html|work=NBA.com|access-date=August 7, 2012}} On October 27, 2012, Orton was released by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], after losing out to 2016 |url-status=dead }} In his first game on February 11, he recorded 16 points and 12 rebounds. After his third game against [[Kia Carnival (PBA team)|Kia Carnival]], he called Kia player-coach (now Senator) [[Manny Pacquiao]] and the game's referees "a joke".[https://www.spin.ph/basketball/news/purefoods-import-daniel-orton-says-manny-pacquiao-playing-in-pba-a-joke-mockery-of-game-rant NBA veteran Daniel Orton goes ballistic, says Manny Pacquiao playing pro hoops 'a joke'], Richard Dy, spin.ph, February 18, 2015 He was summoned by PBA commissioner [[Chito Salud]] two days after the incident and was fined by the commissioner's office [[Philippine Peso|PHP]]250,000 due to his comments.[http://pba.inquirer.net/54115/orton-fined-p250k ORTON FINED P250K], PBA.ph, February 20, 2015 Subsequently, he was sent home by Purefoods' team governor Rene Pardo on February 21.[https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/news/daniel-orton-purefoods-goes-home-rant-manny-pacquiao-fine-kia-philippines-basketball Purefoods sends Daniel Orton home, risks playing all-Filipino as Bowles set for measurement], Richard Dy, spin.ph, February 21, 2015 On March 11, he returned to the D-League, this time joining the [[Grand Rapids Drive]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/daniel-orton-added-to-drives-roster/n-4936486|title=Daniel Orton Added to Drive's Roster|date=March 11, 2015|website=OurSports Central}} On March 26, he was waived by the Drive. He appeared in six games for the Drive, averaging 6.7 points and 5.8 rebounds in 18.3 minutes per game.{{Cite web |url=http://roadtotheassociation.com/2015/03/27/grand-rapids-drive-waive-daniel-orton/
